articles.title: Reyes Owes Daniel Cormier an Apology #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen believes Dominick Reyes owes Daniel Cormier an apology. But what did DC actually say, and was Reyes justified in accusing him of bias? Chael breaks down the controversy surrounding Cormier’s comments about Reyes and fighters from the Caucasus region. In Chael’s view, Daniel wasn’t putting Reyes down or giving him an unfair shake. He was simply acknowledging what he saw: Reyes looked really good. Chael also explains why Cormier referring to Reyes as a “kid” shouldn’t automatically be interpreted as disrespect. Drawing from his own experience with Jon Jones, Chael argues that the context matters—and that Reyes may have been given the wrong impression about what Daniel meant. Ultimately, Chael says he wants to defend Reyes, but he can’t make the case. He believes Daniel Cormier’s hands were clean and that Reyes got this one wrong. Was DC being unfair, or did Reyes misread the situation? articles.title: Sean Strickland Finally Came to His Senses…
articles.description: Sean Strickland finally came to his senses. After questioning whether he wanted to keep competing, Strickland has agreed to face Nassourdine Imavov in February. And Chael Sonnen believes he made the right choice. This was the opponent Sean originally stood up for. When the UFC was looking at a Khamzat Chimaev rematch, Strickland said Imavov deserved the first opportunity. Then Sean had his motorcycle accident, started questioning what he wanted to do, and the entire situation changed. Now he's back. Chael doesn't know what changed between December and February. The opponent is the same. The championship is the same. The only thing that appears to have changed is Sean. Whatever the reason, Chael believes Strickland made the right decision. He's the champion, Imavov earned the opportunity, and now they're going to settle it. Everything is right again. #SeanStrickland #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: There Is NO ONE I Want to See Volkanovski Fight…
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski has a problem: there is nobody I want to see him fight. He’s throwing out Aljamain Sterling at 145, Justin Gaethje at 155, and now Ilia Topuria. When the champion has three different ideas across two divisions, that tells me he doesn’t actually have a fight. Volk says he wants to challenge himself. Fine. Of the three ideas he gave us, there’s one I’ll support: drop the featherweight belt, move to 155 and fight Ilia. You lost to Ilia. You want that one back. You’re both at 155 now. On behalf of the community, we accept. Drop the belt. Go to lightweight. Fight Ilia. articles.title: Did the Judges Get Merab vs. Yan Wrong? #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen was stunned when Petr Yan was awarded the victory over Merab Dvalishvili. Chael explains why he thought Merab won the first three rounds, pointing to the relentless pressure, forward movement, and pace that defined Merab's performance. In Chael's view, Merab continued to push the action through the opening rounds. But one moment stood out: Yan landed a body shot in the third that visibly affected Merab. Merab flinched before smiling, and Chael acknowledges that it was an excellent shot. Even so, he still believed Merab had done enough to win the round. Was that body shot enough to change the round, or did Merab's pressure and activity deserve more credit on the scorecards? Chael breaks down the fight and explains why the decision surprised him. articles.title: Is Islam Makhachev Still the Undisputed Champion? #ufc
articles.description: Is Islam Makhachev still the undisputed UFC champion if an interim champion is crowned? Chael Sonnen raises a question about the UFC's championship system: can a title truly be undisputed when another fighter holds an interim belt in the same division? Chael makes an important distinction. He isn't saying Islam has lost his championship. He's arguing that Islam's status as the *undisputed* champion is now open to debate, because the winner of the interim title fight between Morales and Prates would have a competing claim. Chael also questions why an interim title is being introduced when the situation doesn't appear to involve the usual circumstance of a champion being sidelined by injury. Is this just a matter of terminology, or does an interim belt fundamentally change the meaning of being undisputed? articles.title: Alex Pereira Is NOT a Small Heavyweight
articles.description: Alex Pereira says if heavyweight doesn’t work out, he can go back to 205 because he’s “not a big heavyweight.” I was so surprised by that statement that I questioned whether Pereira had actually said it. My editing team had to send me the proof. Israel Adesanya didn’t like it either. His point was simple: Pereira shouldn’t be making excuses after the Ciryl Gane fight or before he steps in there with Sergei Pavlovich. But there’s another problem—I don’t buy that Pereira is a small heavyweight. He’s taller than most heavyweight champions, has a longer reach than almost all of them and weighs around 240 pounds. If Pereira wins the heavyweight championship, we’ll suddenly be having a very different conversation about where he belongs in the all-time discussion. articles.title: I Was in the Middle of the Arman Tsarukyan–Dillon Danis Brawl
articles.description: RAF 14 had a little bit of everything. Dillon Danis was on fire at the press conference before things got out of control with Arman Tsarukyan and Khamzat Chimaev. What happened afterward impressed me even more. Dillon still had nearly nine pounds to cut, security had been doubled, and there were plenty of reasons he could have walked away. He didn’t. He made the weight and showed up. Jordan Burroughs once again showed why what he’s doing at this stage of his career separates him from the other names in the GOAT conversation. Vito Arujau and Sebastian Rivera produced an incredible comeback, and Jordan Oliver once again refused to pass the torch. articles.title: Volkanovski Just Had One of the DUMBEST Ideas I've Ever Heard
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski is one of the greatest fighters ever. I respect the guy tremendously. But he just laid out one of the dumbest ideas I’ve ever heard. Volk has talked about fighting Justin Gaethje and retiring together. He’s talked about moving to 155 to “test himself” against Ilia Topuria. And then he says he’ll vacate the featherweight belt afterward so he doesn’t hold up the division. What are we doing here? If you really want to test yourself at lightweight, there’s a very simple way to do it: drop the belt now and move into the division without a guaranteed title shot. That’s what Ilia did. That’s what Max Holloway did. Going up only when there’s a championship opportunity waiting for you isn’t the same thing. You want to test yourself? Great. Drop the belt and actually do it. Chapters: 0:00 One of the dumbest ideas I've ever heard 0:30 Gaethje, retire together, gloves down in the middle 0:57 Going to 155 to "test himself" 1:09 96 kilos: Volk is not a natural 145er 1:46 The cop-out: a test only with a title shot waiting 2:02 Drop the belt and go in, like Ilia did 2:19 Do what Max Holloway did: no guarantee 2:36 Challenging Ilia, a guy he already fought 2:54 "I will then vacate the belt": what belt? 3:30 The first Islam fight: he never burned his boats 4:14 Booked to fight at 11 a.m. 4:48 I'm on Volk's side: he just can't promote 5:08 Drop the belt if he beats Ilia? That belt doesn't exist 5:43 Drop it now: come on my show and say it 6:00 Wanting Gaethje is not testing yourself #UFC #MMA #AlexanderVolkanovski #JustinGaethje #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Islam Makhachev Was Offered Prates… I’m Surprised He Said No
articles.description: Matt Brown and Henry Cejudo both came out in support of Islam Makhachev, but I think they’re arguing against something Islam never actually said. Islam didn’t reject Carlos Prates because he wanted an easier opponent or more time between fights. His issue was the date because of Ramadan. That distinction matters. But there’s a bigger question here. Islam previously told me he wanted two more fights: Michael Morales and Shavkat Rakhmonov. Those are two of the hardest guys he could possibly call out. So I was surprised to hear he was offered Prates. And if Islam believes Morales and Rakhmonov are the harder fights, what exactly is wrong with taking Prates? If the money is the same and you believe he’s the easier opponent, take the fight. That’s your job. Chapters: 0:00 Matt Brown: Islam has earned the right to fight less 0:47 Cejudo agrees: let Prates and Morales fight first 1:32 “I don't think you read the article” 1:41 What Islam actually said: it was the date 2:35 MMA copied boxing's worst habits 4:06 Give a guy 12 months, everyone takes 12 months 4:26 The Mayweather challenge 5:20 If the champion won't walk out, use an interim title 5:51 First champion to miss a date without saying hurt or sick 6:35 Why Islam wasn't stripped: the Ramadan tying 7:22 Islam said two more: Morales and Rakhmonov, then out 7:54 Surprised by the Prates offer 8:36 Jon Jones has one left, why wait? 9:21 Final thought: if Prates isn't the hardest, why not take him? #UFC #MMA #IslamMakhachev #CarlosPrates #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Islam can NOT be Undisputed Champion…
articles.description: The UFC has announced Carlos Prates vs. Michael Morales for an interim championship while Islam Makhachev remains the undisputed champion—and I have a problem with the terminology. By definition, how can an interim champion exist alongside an undisputed champion? We saw a version of this before with Tom Aspinall and Jon Jones, but Islam’s situation raises a different question. Islam isn’t out because of an injury or illness. If Prates or Morales becomes interim champion, doesn’t that mean Islam’s championship is now disputed? I wouldn’t necessarily have handled the situation differently. But the question remains: Is Islam Makhachev still the undisputed champion? Chapters: 0:00 Trying to understand the Islam news 0:36 The Aspinall and Jones night: an interim champion in the presence of an undisputed champion 1:55 Tom Aspinall told me I was the only one saying it 3:06 Prates vs. Morales gets announced for the interim championship 3:48 Can an undisputed champion exist alongside an interim champion? 5:07 You don't do an interim belt unless the champion is out 6:18 Islam is not fighting due to Ramadan: a very sticky subject 7:12 An interim title fight while the undisputed champion has no illness or injury 8:36 Islam's candid statement: they wanted me to fight Prates 9:25 Is Islam still the undisputed champion, or has he been demoted? #UFC #MMA #IslamMakhachev #Welterweight #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Volkanovski vs. Gaethje Is a TERRIBLE Idea
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski has a habit of making his career harder than it needs to be. Instead of chasing the easiest matchup and biggest payday, Volk consistently looks for the guy who has earned the opportunity. But this time, he may have gotten something exactly right. Volkanovski wants to beat Movsar Evloev and then move to 155 for a retirement fight against Justin Gaethje. I initially thought the idea had virtually no chance of happening. Then Volk's camp offered an alternative: if he doesn't get Gaethje, he'll stay at featherweight and defend against Aljamain Sterling. Those are two very different nights of business for the UFC. Whether Volk intended it as leverage or not, he may have just played his strongest card. #UFC #MMA #AlexanderVolkanovski #JustinGaethje #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Does ONE Liver Shot Win a Round?
articles.description: Petr Yan landed the best shot of the third round against Merab Dvalishvili, a body shot that clearly hurt him. But was that one shot enough to win the entire round? That’s what I’m trying to understand. Take that body shot away, and I think Merab clearly won the round on pressure, output, takedowns, and control. All three judges gave the round to Yan. The rules prioritize damage, but what exactly qualifies as damage? Is visibly hurting your opponent enough? Does damage have to leave something we can actually see? I’m not claiming the judges got it wrong. I’m asking how we’re supposed to apply the standard consistently. I had Merab winning three rounds to two. #UFC #MMA #MerabDvalishvili #PetrYan #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Alexander Volkov Deserves Our Support
articles.description: Alexander Volkov has the wins, the record, and the ranking. What I’ve been waiting for is for him to actually make some noise and advocate for himself. He finally did it. Then he went out and won. Volkov has been there for a long time. Now I think it’s time for the MMA community to put some wind in his sails. articles.description: Dana White: UFC 333 Post-Fight Press Conference Dana White’s full UFC 333 post-fight press conference from Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. White announced the highest attendance and biggest gate for a UFC event in Abu Dhabi history, called Alexander Volkanovski “an absolute stud” after his finish of previously unbeaten Movsar Evloev, and said Merab Dvalishvili “couldn’t have fought a better fight” in his trilogy loss to Petr Yan. White also explained why Islam Makhachev’s situation led to an interim title fight in Toronto, addressed Shakur Stevenson’s release from Zuffa Boxing, said he and the matchmakers were texting all night about Song Yadong and Sean O’Malley as Yan’s next opponent, and answered questions on Dillon Danis, RAF, Farid Basharat, a UFC event in Russia and his next “unique” event. articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski: UFC 333 Post-Fight Press Conference | SICK and Still Finished Evloev
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski’s full UFC 333 post-fight press conference after his second-round finish of previously unbeaten Movsar Evloev in Abu Dhabi. Volkanovski broke down how he let Evloev’s wrestling wear him out, revealed he was sick on fight day, and said a lightweight super fight with Justin Gaethje is “something I would retire for”: win or lose, he’d retire and vacate so he isn’t holding the division up. He also responded to Petr Yan wanting to move up for a fight with him, said Evloev is “the toughest challenge for everyone in the division,” gave his advice to Merab Dvalishvili, and explained the strict 10-week diet behind his longevity at 38. articles.title: This was NOT Knockout of the Year!
articles.description: MMA Weekly believes a wild regional MMA finish could be the knockout of the year, but Chael Sonnen isn't buying it. After watching a fighter knock out his opponent by jumping backward while carrying him on his back, Chael questions whether a finish you can't even see or intentionally reproduce should qualify. And there's another problem: on the very same weekend, Mike Malott delivered a devastating knee that sent Joaquin Buckley's mouthpiece flying. Chael asks the obvious question: how can something be knockout of the year if it wasn't even the best knockout of the weekend? articles.title: ‘BODY SHOT!’ DJ Reacts To Merab vs Yan
Daniel Cormier REACTS to Alexander Volkanovski TKO win vs. Evloev, Petr Yan BEATS Merab Dvalishvili
articles.description: Daniel Cormier IS BACK LIVE from the octagon in Abu Dhabi after UFC 333's incredible main event championship fights, with Alexander Volkanovski FINISHING Movsar Evloev in the 2nd round via TKO and Petr Yan beating Merab Dvalishvili by unanimous decision! DC gives his reaction to Volk getting an incredible win over the undefeated 20-0 Evloev, and what's next for the 38-year-old champion and arguably the greatest featherweight in UFC history. Cormier also dives into what was an incredible co-main event between Merab and Petr Yan, where Yan once again defeated Merab on his way to a successful title defense! Cormier also gives his take on the latest with Islam Makhachev, Carlos Prates, and Michael Morales, as well as what's next for the heavyweight division with Alexander Volkov's convincing victory. And don't miss DC give his take on Aaron Pico's first-round finish, Lone'er Kavanagh's nasty first round TKO, and some incredible prelims including Dominic Reyes' first round win!
